items.text: Command line on Linux and macOS: read pages (including open unsaved edits), journals, blocks and linked references, search, run queries, list pages and check the graph's owner, with text or `--json` output. Read commands use the app when it has the graph open; otherwise they start `tine serve`, which hands over when the app opens it. These commands do not edit notes. On Windows the owner endpoint is unavailable: reads and `serve` report `unsupported` and exit 5; the app still opens graphs normally. The Guide's **Command line** page explains usage and scripting output.

items.text: Android: Tine appears in the share sheet. Shared text, links and images become a new block at the bottom of today's journal, the same place quick capture files to, with the same "Captured to today's journal" notice. If an item can't be added yet, for example because no graph is open or saving fails, Tine keeps it and retries the next time it opens. A retry never loses the item; it can add it twice only if Tine is closed or crashes right after the journal was saved, or when an old share is reopened from Android's recent apps after Tine was closed. A share Tine can't save whole (more than 32 images, a file over 64 MiB, a non-image file, a file from Tine itself) is refused with a message instead of being saved in part (GH #608, REG-GH608-SHARE-INBOX-EXACTLY-ONCE).

regressionEvidence.reason: Catalog rows REG-GH608-SHARE-INBOX-EXACTLY-ONCE, REG-GH608-ANDROID-SHARE-TARGET are covered.

docs.reason: Platforms and mobile describes the Android share sheet, retry and refusal behavior.

items.text: Saving moved into one background page host per graph: every edit is saved as you type, from any window, and keeps saving after the page closes. If a file changes on disk while you have unsaved text on that page, the page shows a comparison where you keep your edits or take the disk version, block by block. Unsaved text survives a crash: the next start puts it back on its page, saves it, and names each recovered page; it is never written over a file that changed meanwhile. Closing the last window while a page still cannot be saved reopens the graph and names those pages instead of quitting. Switching graphs waits until a running rename finishes.

items.text: Graph settings: when `logseq/config.edn` disappears while a graph is open (iCloud offloading it, a sync tool replacing it), Tine keeps the settings it read, as Logseq does, instead of switching to the defaults. Before, namespace pages could show as `xxx___yyy` and new ones were written under Logseq's old file names. A graph whose `config.edn` is still in iCloud and not downloaded opens read-only rather than with guessed settings (REG-OG-CONFIG-VANISH-KEEPS-FORMAT).

docs.reason: Bug fix restoring Logseq behavior when config.edn disappears; the Guide's live config.edn text is unchanged. The read-only open for an undownloaded iCloud config is an edge case with no Guide text today.
